content.value_statement: Intermediate learners often know grammar but struggle to sound natural in real Chinese conversations. This skill analyzes expressions, rewrites drafts, and adds usage evidence for better phrasing.
actual_capabilities: Explains when a Chinese expression is casual, formal, spoken, or written.
Compares textbook wording with more natural native-style phrasing.
Suggests alternate expressions with tone, frequency, and context notes.
Rewrites Chinese drafts for smoother rhythm and clearer communication.
Guides web searches for real examples from Weibo, bilibili, Zhihu, and similar sources.
Provides Japanese explanations for HSK4 and higher Chinese learners.
limitations: It is not a certified language teacher or exam grader.
Current usage examples require web access and source checking.
It needs the user to state audience, purpose, and desired formality for best edits.
It may not cover every regional use across mainland China, Taiwan, and diaspora communities.

use_cases.title: Analyze a new expression
use_cases.description: Understand where a phrase appears, who uses it, and whether it fits a conversation.
use_cases.target_user: HSK4 learners reading social posts or video comments

use_cases.title: Rewrite a chat message
use_cases.description: Turn a correct but stiff sentence into a natural message for friends or classmates.

use_cases.title: Improve longer writing
use_cases.description: Review an essay or translation for flow, word choice, and native-style expression.

prompt_templates.title: Explain one phrase
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the phrase "搞定了". Explain when to use it, who can use it, and one safer alternative.

prompt_templates.title: Compare similar expressions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare "有意思", "有点儿意思", and "挺有意思的". Explain tone, formality, and common situations.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a message
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this Chinese message for a close friend. Keep it casual and natural: 我昨天去了电影院，看了一个很好的电影。

prompt_templates.title: Audit a full draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Chinese paragraph for naturalness, flow, and register. Give better versions, reasons, and real usage examples when possible.

output_examples.output: The phrase is casual and spoken. It means something is finished or handled. Use it with friends, classmates, or coworkers in relaxed settings.

output_examples.input: Improve: 我认为这个电影非常有意思。
output_examples.output: A more natural version is 这电影挺有意思的. It sounds lighter, more conversational, and better suited to casual comments.

output_examples.input: Explain whether "非常感谢" is natural in chat.
output_examples.output: It is correct, but it can sound formal. In casual chat, 太谢谢你了 or 谢谢你帮忙 often sounds warmer.

best_practices: Provide the full sentence, audience, and channel before asking for corrections.
Ask for formality and tone comparisons when several expressions seem similar.
Check cited examples before reusing slang, regional phrases, or recent internet expressions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a single perfect translation without giving context.
Do not use casual rewrites in business or academic settings without checking register.
Do not treat web examples as correct unless the source and context are reliable.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for HSK4 and higher learners who want more natural Chinese for reading, chatting, and writing.

faq.question: Can it correct grammar?
faq.answer: Yes, but it focuses first on naturalness, tone, rhythm, and real communication.

faq.question: Does it require web search?
faq.answer: Web search is useful for fresh examples from social platforms, comments, and articles. Static explanation can still work without it.

faq.question: Can it explain internet slang?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain slang, but recent slang should be checked against current sources.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.

faq.question: Will it make writing sound native every time?
faq.answer: No. It improves phrasing and explains tradeoffs, but native feedback is still valuable for important writing.
